title: Compress all log files older than 7 days with gzip
summary: Find the .log files in a folder that have not changed for more than a week, then compress each one into a .gz file. Names with spaces are handled safely.

aliases.text: find all logs older than 7 days and gzip them
compress logs older than a week linux
find old files and compress them
archive old log files to save disk space
найти логи старше 7 дней и сжать их gzip

steps.explain: Preview first. This only lists the .log files whose content changed more than 7 days ago. Nothing is changed yet.
steps.expect: One path per line, for example logs/app-2026-10-01.log. No output means no file is old enough.

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder that holds the log files

steps.explain: Compress each listed file. find -print0 and xargs -0 pass names separated by zero bytes, so spaces are safe. xargs -r skips gzip if nothing matched. Each X.log becomes X.log.gz and the original is removed.
steps.expect: Usually no output. The old .log files disappear and .log.gz files appear next to them.

placeholders.name: LOG_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder that holds the log files

steps.explain: Check the result: list the compressed files. Each one should have the same name as before plus .gz.
steps.expect: Paths ending in .log.gz, for example logs/app-2026-10-01.log.gz

rollback.explain: Restore the plain text files. gunzip removes each .gz file and writes the original name back. It also unpacks any .log.gz file that was already there before.

warnings: gzip removes each original .log file and keeps only the .gz version. Copy the folder first if you may need the plain text.
-mtime +7 means the file's content was last changed more than 7 days ago, not that it was created then.
Run the preview step and check the list before compressing.
